newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares fall sharply amid unrest.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares fall sharply amid unrest.

text.p: Israeli shares fell across the board in thin trading following clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops in which nearly 70 people have been killed.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 2.30 percent, or 4.34 points, to 184.28. The Maof 25 index dropped 2.23 percent to 193.08.
Sunday's closing volume was not available because trading of shares in the Karam index of small cap stocks had not finished yet.
"The events had a very negative impact on investors and most of them are sitting on the fence," said a trader at Bank Leumi.
The Tel Aviv bourse closed two hours early on Sunday and will do so throughout the week due to the Jewish holiday of Succoth. Normal trading hours will resume on October 6.

"We were expecting a correction following Thursday's sharp decline but the market continued to fall. There are rumours that foreign investors started selling today," said Yoram Ben-Yaeir at Ahrayut Investment Management.
Israel's opening of a controversial tunnel near holy sites in Jerusalem last week sparked clashes in which 55 Palestinans and 14 Israeli soldiers have been killed.
Despite declines in the market, Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, the most active share, rose 4.25 percent to 145,462 on high turnover of 13 million shekels.

Other active shares included Elite Industries, which lost 0.75 percent to 1,241 on turnover of 4.7 million shekels and Koor Industries, which fell 3.0 percent to 27,692 on turnover of 4.0 million shekels.
